title: GPU kernel probe synthesis + upgrade roadmap
content:
Status: draft synthesis + actionable checklist.

Purpose:
- Capture a concise compatibility synthesis across K8s versions, NVIDIA driver versions, CUDA and NCCL combos we care about for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Propose an upgrade/validation roadmap and a small probe harness + Terraform notes to roll forward with minimal customer disruption.
- Surface open questions and next steps for QE and SRE pairing.

High-level constraints/assumptions:
- Primary supported GPU types: A100 (40/80), H100 (selected clusters), and V100 (legacy).
- Private customers often pin K8s (1.26 -> 1.28 range) and expect driver upgrades without node replacement when possible.
- We prefer maintaining a single driver family per cluster (driver containers + daemonset) to limit operational complexity.

Quick compatibility synthesis (summary row):
- K8s 1.25-1.28: works with NVIDIA driver 535.x and 545.x but kernel ABI regressions observed on RHEL 8.8 with 545.
- CUDA 12.1: stable with NCCL 2.18 for throughput workloads on A100; H100 shows memory probe flakiness at long seq lengths when using 545 drivers.
- CUDA 11.8: still supported for legacy V100 stacks with driver 525.x. NCCL 2.12 recommended there.

Representative ASCII matrix (short):
K8s | Driver | CUDA | NCCL | Notes
-----|--------|------|------|------
1.25 | 525.105 | 11.8 | 2.12 | V100 stable, prefer pinned quantization builds
1.26 | 535.86  | 12.0 | 2.15 | A100 validated, default for many clusters
1.27 | 535.86  | 12.1 | 2.18 | A100 H100 mixed clusters OK but run probe (see tests)
1.28 | 545.45  | 12.1 | 2.18 | RHEL kernel ABI risk; run kernel-module smoke tests

Note: full matrix in spreadsheet (linked_artifacts). This doc focuses on an opinionated upgrade path + validation probes.

Probe harness (short-run tests to gate driver+cuda upgrades):
- Goals: verify node-level driver install, device visibility, CUDA runtime smoke, NCCL ring formation across 2-8 pods, and long-run stability (30m) with streaming generation workload.

Core checks (ordered):
1) Node-level sanity
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,compute_mode --format=csv
   - check /proc/driver/nvidia/version and dmesg for module errors
2) Driver container install (DaemonSet) smoke: create a privileged pod that mounts /var/lib and checks module load/unload using modprobe and insmod fallback
3) CUDA runtime: run a minimal deviceQuery (cuda-samples) inside a container built with the target CUDA runtime (12.1 / 11.8). Expect device count match nvidia-smi.
4) NCCL ring formation: run nccl-tests/all_reduce across N pods (N=2,4,8), verify consistent throughput and no timeout failures.
5) Persistent KV cache check: run a small LLM inference workload (2 tokens/sec sustained) for 30 minutes to watch for OOM or RMM errors.
6) Kernel-module stress: run dkms-like unload/load cycles (if kernel supports) and check dmesg for WARN/CRITICAL.

Failure modes we watch for:
- Module Oops / taint messages in dmesg immediately after install.
- Inconsistent device visibility across kubelets (one node shows 0 GPUs).
- NCCL timeouts linking peers (common with mixed driver families).
- CUDA driver mismatch errors (libcuda.so vs driver mismatch).
- Kernel ABI mismatch errors on RHEL kernels (notably customer clusters running custom kernel-rt builds).

Terraform module notes (short):
- goal: add an opt-in driver lifecycle resource to infra/terraform/modules/gpu-nodepool to allow: pre-drain -> install -> post-health-check -> uncordon pattern.
- Minimal resource interface prototype:
  - resource "redwood_gpu_driver" {
      node_pool_id = string
      driver_version = string
      strategy = "daemonset|node-image|pkg-manager"
    }
- Implementation guidance: prefer daemonset-based driver install for clouds where kernel packaging is stable (GCP/Azure). For on-prem with strict host images, expose a node-image path and a rollback image tag.
- Safety: always include a canary set size (e.g., 2 nodes) and a max-concurrent-upgrades variable.

Proposed upgrade sequence (canary -> rollout):
1) Create agentless smoke pool: provision 2 nodes with same image and taint so they don't get user traffic. Install new driver version and run probe harness.
2) If pass, mark nodepool canary and run workload-level A/B tests for 2 hours (generate synthetic traces).
3) If canary good, incrementally upgrade remaining nodes with max_concurrent=1 or 2 depending on cluster size, running 10m of smoke tests post-upgrade each node.
4) If failure in step, automated rollback: drain node, re-image/roll back driver, rejoin. Postmortem capturing kernel logs and kubectl describe events.

Rollback playbook (quick):
- immediate: cordon affected node(s), scale down stateful pods with graceful termination.
- gather: kubectl get pods -o wide, nvidia-smi, dmesg > /tmp/driver-failure-logs.tar.gz, collect /var/log/messages.
- revert: use terraform apply with driver_version set to previous stable tag or reimage node pool (uses node-image parameter).
- validate: re-run probe harness on reverted nodes before uncordon.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Kernel ABI policy: do we maintain a tested kernel matrix per supported distro (Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky) or publish explicit "kernel ABI unsupported" warnings for customers running custom kernels?
- Do we support in-place module replacement on H100 clusters or do we require node reboots as a policy? (H100 driver stack has historically needed reboot on 545+)
- How to report mixed-driver cluster health in Console? Proposed quick signal: a per-node driver_version label + cluster-level metric for mismatched-driver-count.

Short-term action items (next 2 sprints):
- [ ] Implement probe harness as a lightweight helm chart + Job (owner: Asha) - target: PoC in staging by 2026-01-15.
- [ ] Prototype terraform resource for driver lifecycle (owner: Marcus) - PR by 2026-01-30.
- [ ] QE to author 6 canonical validation jobs (owner: Priya) - include kernel stress, nccl ring, 30m LLM run.
- [ ] SRE to test canary workflow on internal dev cluster (owner: Evan) - run two canaries across Ubuntu+RHEL nodes.

Notes to self / TODOs to expand later:
- Collect historical incident IDs where driver upgrade led to customer downtime (search: ENG-).
- Add a short customer-facing doc summarizing upgrade SLO and expected O(1) disruption window.
- Coordinate with Console team to get the driver mismatched metric and label UI added to the kube node details page.

References/commands (handy):
- device query: docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
- nccl test: docker run --rm --gpus all nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/nccl-tests:2.15_mpich ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 1
- kernel logs quick: journalctl -k --no-pager | tail -n 200
- probe job example (k8s): kubectl run gpu-probe --image=redwood/probe:canary --restart=OnFailure --limits='{"nvidia.com/gpu":"1"}' -- /bin/sh -c "/opt/probe/run-smoke.sh"

If we converge on the sequence above, next step is to draft the Terraform PR and the helm chart skeleton. Keep this doc as living notes; will move polished playbook to Confluence once owners sign-off.

-- Riley
